children: Overview
Canada photonic quantum computing firm's Q3 revenue rose 32% yr/yr, driven by DARPA and partnerships
Net loss widened to $32.2 mln as R&D and G&A expenses increased
Company secured $140 mln in Canadian government funding and $10 mln DARPA extension for R&D
Outlook
Company targets year-end 2026 system loss of 10.2
Xanadu aims for up to 200 logical qubits by 2029, 500 by 2030, and 1,000 by 2031
Result Drivers
R&D INVESTMENT - Higher engineering headcount and material costs drove a 67% yr/yr increase in R&D expense, supporting accelerated cycles of learning and component progress
GOVERNMENT AND PARTNERSHIP FUNDING - Revenue growth was primarily driven by DARPA QBI revenue and partnership engagements, though offset by completion of prior-year contracts
TECHNOLOGY ADVANCEMENTS - Progress in reducing system loss and new component records supported advancement toward year-end system loss targets and long-term quantum computing goals
